en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, has shaggy crest feathers and weighs up to eight kilograms, making it one of the world's largest eagles.
Jose Rizal wrote his final poem, Mi Ultimo Adios, hidden inside an alcohol cooking stove that his sister smuggled out of his prison cell.
The Philippine Supreme Court has exactly fifteen justices, including the Chief Justice, who must all retire at the mandatory age of seventy.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over two thousand years ago using only hand tools, carving steps into mountains without modern machinery.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a makeshift incubator using two native bamboo baskets.
The Baybayin script, used by ancient Filipinos before the Spanish arrived, was traditionally carved on bamboo or leaves rather than written on paper.
During the Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, participants cover their bodies with black soot to honor the indigenous Ati people and the Santo Nino.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, while the national flag was officially unfurled for the very first time.
The Sampaguita, our national flower, is a jasmine species that blooms most fragrant at night to attract its specific moth pollinators.
The Filipino concept of Bayanihan originated from the literal practice of a community carrying a traditional nipa hut on bamboo poles to a new location.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo painted his famous rural scenes using a unique technique of backlighting, where the sun shines from behind his subjects.
The Philippine flag is the only national flag flown with the red stripe on top to signify the country is in a state of war.
